title: Three Years and One Short Ribbon
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（人与自我·做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（人与自我·做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：medal　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 medal 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the athlete ① won the medal that no coach in the gym would have recorded, and he said the winning was the whole of the year. The ② medal, meaning the honour itself and not the ribbon, ran three years and stayed unrecorded in the book; a medal, he said, is the only thing in a gym that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ medal in that gym had the same short ribbon beside it, and the ④ medal at the far podium, meaning the title they kept for the children to see and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A medal, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the athlete said the recording is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the medal was the whole of the matter, meaning the effort and not the honour. The ⑥ medal, meaning the effort and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; medal, he said, is either something you win or the only word that means both an honour and an effort. He said the effort is the part they remember.

By 1992 the ⑦ medal had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short ribbon. The ⑧ medal of the whole thing, the athlete wrote in August, was one gym and three years of recording; medal, he said, is either the title at the far podium or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ medal I remember is the honour recorded in the list, which closed in 1994 and is still recorded as the quietest in the gym. A ⑩ medal, my mother said in 1996, is the only honour that improves by being recorded; every medal, she said, is an effort that has agreed to look like an honour. She said the effort was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 奖牌；勋章（指体育馆里每一枚旁边的那一枚）
B. n. 奖牌；勋章（指那枚奖牌本身，与绶带相对）
C. 固定搭配：win the medal 赢得这枚奖牌
D. n. 奖牌；勋章（指留给孩子们看的那一枚那一枚）
E. n. 争牌之事（抽象总称，指一处体育馆的奖牌之事）
F. n. 奖牌；勋章（指获奖名录里写到、被记载的的那一枚）
G. n. 功绩、付出（指一件事里人人都拼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 付出（抽象总称，指人人都拼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: won the medal that no coach in the gym would have recorded
The medal, meaning the honour itself and not the ribbon
the medal at the far podium
the medal was the whole of the matter
the medal had become a line in a list
The medal of the whole thing
A medal, my mother said in 1996

answers.why: win the medal 意为“赢得这枚奖牌”，1987 年那位运动员把体育馆里没有一位教练肯记载的一枚奖牌做了一遍。
medal 意为“奖牌；勋章”，指那枚奖牌本身而不是绶带，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被记载。
medal 意为“奖牌；勋章”，指体育馆里每一枚旁边的那一枚，每一枚旁边都有同一条小小的绶带。
medal 意为“奖牌；勋章”，指最远那座领奖台留给孩子们看的那一枚那一枚，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
medal 意为“功绩、付出”，指一件事里人人都拼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份功绩就是那件事的全部。
medal 意为“付出”，指人人都拼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那枚奖牌，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
medal 意为“奖牌；勋章”，指获奖名录里写到、被记载的的那一枚，到 1992 年这一枚成了获奖名录里的一行。
medal 意为“争牌之事”，运动员八月写道，整件事的奖牌之事是一处体育馆和三个年份的记载。
medal 意为“奖牌；勋章”，我记得的是获奖名录里记载过的那一枚，1994 年领完了，至今仍被说成体育馆里最安静的一枚。
medal 为抽象总称，母亲 1996 年说，奖牌是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的奖牌。
